I frequently see people asking many questions about a good dosage to get high on suboxone. What I say next is very important.

**If you are not strongly opiate tolerant, a small dose of suboxone will make you VERY sick. A large dose could put you out for days. You can't throw it up or expel it, it's very strong. Imagine a time you drank too much alcohol and was puking your guts out, and multiply it times 10 and then you can imagine a suboxone OD.**

------------------------

For those who are currently on opiates and looking to suboxone for maintance relief you may need a high dose at start to keep you feeling well. It depends on your habit. Once you are fully on suboxone I recommend a small dose twice a day. 2-mg twice a day is the best dose for me. Now many people think the doctor prescribed me 8-mgs 2 times a day, why shouldn't I take that much or more?

It's an easy answer. According to the FDA and SAMSHA suboxone has a ceiling dose of 16-mg and anything higher will discontinue giving any feeling of relief or being high. Now I have found that for myself the ceiling dose is much much **less** at 4-mg. It's probably different for all of us, but for me a 4-mg dose feels the exact same as a 16-mg dose.

There's another part to this as well. In my many experiences I've found that taking large doses (anything over 4-mg at once) will leave me with much stronger withdrawal symptoms when I wake up and require my new dose. But if I stay at my 2-4 mg dose twice a day, **I WILL NOT EXPERIENCE ANY WITHDRAWAL SYMPTOMS IN THE MORNING!!!**

I don't know the science behind that but it makes sense to me. If I compare withdrawal symptoms for the next day after I used a small amount of dope to a different day when I used a large amount of dope, I would have significantly worse withdrawals from the day when I used the large amount. ---------------------- And let me finish with a bit of the science I do know about. When you ingest the suboxone (buprenorphine & naloxone) the buprenorphine is metabolized by the liver via the cytochrome P4503A4 enzyme system into **norbuprenorphine** and other metabolites.

Now the buprenorphine doesn't have much ability to get you high because it is a partial agonist. It does a good job taking care of the physical, but not the mental.

Now **norbuprenorphine** (the metabolite) is a full antagonist, and can give you a small feeling of euphoria. It's not like heroin, just a feeling like you *just received some good news* and it also has to compete with the buprenorphine already glued to the receptors. Of course the norbuprenorphine has a better chance of reacting many hours after your dose when the buprenorphine is fading away.

So this is my experience mixed together with some science, and I leave you with this:

Taking smaller doses of suboxone will save you money, help you feel better, and maybe even get you higher. Of course I might be completely wrong, but it works for me. Also for those in judgement right now, it's not like I found some new way to get high. I just might feel a little bit of euphoria on my lower dose.

**Disclaimer: DO NOT MENTION ANY OF THIS TO YOUR SUBOXONE DOCTOR. They get paid and kickbacks and threats from the pharmaceutical industry to keep us on high doses. If you choose to take a lower dose like me, then do so in silence. And keep those extras for those sure to come rainy fucking days.**

I'm bringing up Windows 10 Insider Preview on my Mac on Parallels Desktop 8 right now. Not a big Windows user any more, but I will evaluate everything I can.

  4. The install makes a one time offer to choose an Azure or Windows domain. I chose the personal option. It appears that switching is not easy.

  5. After logging, and sitting idle for a few moments, an Insider Hub pops up. Gamification? There's something about Quests and Achievements Unlocked. WTF?

  6. There's a start button. Huh. Launches the Windows 8 UI in a Window.

  7. Settings. "You need to verify your identity on this device." WTF? Click. Crash. Relaunch. Now it works. I didn't know that my live.com account was linked with my gmail. So it sends a code to the other email id. There are other options, but I don't want to try them out yet.

  10. It's slow, but usable. I can test it without expending another laptop on this.
